2026.EP21.9.t: Recognition of Staff at Exhibition Place - United Way Campaign and Community Events Program
2026.EP21.9.s:
Exhibition Place employee recognized by the Board for recent outstanding accomplishment:

1. 2025 United Way City of Toronto Campaign

Each year, to build a better city, the City of Toronto Public Service Staff, along with all Agencies, Boards, and Commissions participate in the annual city-wide fundraising program in support of United Way Toronto and York Region campaigns.

Exhibition Place raised a grand total of $1,017.35 for the United Way of Toronto Campaign. In 2025 we focused our efforts on Old Technology Sales and the annual Ghost Walk Program. Over the last 21 years Exhibition Place has contributed $101,785.78 to the United Way Toronto and York Region campaigns.

2. 2025 Community Events Program

Exhibition Place ran a collection of low-cost community events, where attendees would pay what they can to attend these events during the spring and summer months.

Exhibition Place raised a grand total of $2,754.76 from our cumulative Community Events program organized during the spring and summer months: Yoga in the Park, Beekeeping, Pencil Sketching Techniques, Shape the Scene – A journey from Block-In to Detail, Draw Simplified Buildings with Lines and Values at the Horse Palace, Create a Story in Your Draw Urban Sketching at the Garden of the Greek Gods.</p…

2026.EP22.1.t: Cybersecurity Audit of Exhibition Place - Phase Two: Overall Network Security and Cybersecurity Assessment of Select Critical Systems
2026.EP22.1.s:
The Auditor General included a cybersecurity audit of Exhibition Place, an agency of the City of Toronto, in her 2025 Work Plan. Exhibition Place is Canada’s largest convention centre and entertainment and sports venue, generating $595 million[1] in economic impact annually and $67.3 million in revenue in 2024.

Phase One of this cybersecurity audit was presented at Exhibition Place’s December 5, 2025, Board meeting. The Auditor General’s Phase One confidential report included results from testing physical security, user access management, and staff awareness of social engineering in relation to cybersecurity. The Phase One public cover report is available at:

Cybersecurity Audit of Exhibition Place – Phase One: Physical Security, User Access Management and Staff Training

Technology plays a vital role in all aspects of Exhibition Place's operations and services. This Phase Two report includes the results of our vulnerability assessment and penetration testing of the Exhibition Place’s network, systems, applications and devices, as well as cybersecurity incident logging and monitoring review.

This report includes five administrative recommendations. The confidential findings and recommendations are contained in Confidential Attachment …
2026.EP22.1.r:
The Auditor General recommends that the Board of Governors of Exhibition Place:

1. Adopt the Confidential Recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1.

2. Subject to City Council approval, direct that Confidential Attachment 1 be released at the discretion of the Auditor General, after discussions with the appropriate Exhibition Place and City officials.

3. Direct the Confidential Attachment 2 remain confidential in its entirety, as it pertains to the security of the property of the City of Toronto or one of its agencies and corporations.

4. Forward this report and Confidential Attachment 1 to City Council for information through the City's Audit Committee.

5. Recommend that City Council authorize the public release of Confidential Attachment 1 at the discretion of the Auditor General, after discussions with the appropriate Exhibition Place and City officials.

2026.EP22.2.t: High Voltage Feeders A34T and A35T Central Replacement at Exhibition Place
2026.EP22.2.s:
This report recommends approving a contract with Black & McDonald Limited of Scarborough, Ontario, for the replacement of high voltage feeders (cables) A34T and A35T. The tender for this contract was issued on February 9, 2026, through Exhibition Place Purchasing and Materials Stores via the Bonfire Online Procurement System, and the recommendation is to award the contract to the lowest compliant bidder meeting tender requirements and specifications within the available budget.

This project is time-sensitive in meeting stakeholders and operational requirements. The existing underground electrical infrastructure is over seventy (70) years old and requires replacement. This project is part of a program that started four years ago to address unanticipated power outages and failures caused by obsolete underground electrical infrastructure.

The Chair of the Board in consultation with the Chief Executive Officer of Exhibition Place approved this contract award on March 4, 2026, pursuant to the authority under the Board Financial By-law 2-18, Article X and seek concurrence of the Board.

2026.EP22.7.s:
This report presents a summary and analysis of grievance and arbitration activity for 2025, along with a comparison with previous years. Exhibition Place has seven (7) collective agreements to which it is bound on the grounds. In 2025, the total number of grievances filed by all bargaining units on Exhibition Place grounds was sixteen (16), compared with six (6) in 2024. There were no arbitrations in 2025.

LiUNA 506 filed five (5) grievances, and Carpenters 27 submitted one (1) grievance, with all grievances either resolved or withdrawn.

IATSE 58 filed ten (10) grievances, of which one (1) was resolved. Nine (9) of the grievances from IATSE relate to a specific event or originate from a tenanted facility. The remaining grievance concerns the assignment of work and the scope of jurisdiction.

2026.EP22.10.t: Exhibition Place - Vision Plan and Concept Scenario Presentation
2026.EP22.10.s:
In response to the various developments at and around Exhibition Place, staff, in collaboration with Studio tla, have developed the Exhibition Place - Vision Plan and Concept Scenario (the Vision Plan). This work considers the different needs of multiple transformative change proposals for the grounds while ensuring alignment with the recommendations of previous studies and plans, including the latest Next Place – Exhibition Place Master Plan approved by Council.

The Chief Executive Officer will present the Vision Plan attached as Attachment A.
2026.EP22.10.r:
The Chief Executive Officer, Exhibition Place, recommends that the Board of Governors of Exhibition Place:

1. Endorse in principle the Exhibition Place - Vision Plan and Concept Scenario (the Vision Plan) in Attachment A.

2. Direct the Chief Executive Officer to work with the City Manager, City Chief Financial Officer, and other relevant city divisions on planning and financing options to advance the concept to fruition, and to report back to the Board on progress by the first quarter of 2027.

2026.EP22.15.t: Ontario Line Update - Presentation by Metrolinx
2026.EP22.15.s:
Announced by the Province of Ontario in 2019, the Ontario Line is one of four priority transit projects being led by Metrolinx in the Greater Toronto Area (GTA). It represents the largest single expansion in Toronto’s subway history, aimed at reducing congestion on existing transit lines and extending service to underserved neighbourhoods across the city.

The Ontario Line will add 15.6 kilometres of new subway service to Toronto, improving the speed, convenience, and connectivity of transit across the city. Stretching from Exhibition Place in the west to the future Eglinton Crosstown LRT at Don Mills Road and Eglinton Avenue East, the line will include 15 stations - six of which will serve as interchange stations - and provide more than 40 new connections to GO trains, existing subway lines, streetcars, and bus services.

Since the Board’s last update in April 2025, construction at Exhibition Station has advanced significantly. Work over the past year has included completion of the Early Works project, completion of excavation for the Exhibition Portal, north main entrance building and traction power substation, completion of piling for the future station platforms, and completion of portal waterproofing and concrete pours.

Construction is also continuing on several major elements of the project. Tunnel boring machine assembly has started and remains ongoing, as has construction of the TBM logi…

2026.EP24.5.t: Recognition of Staff at Exhibition Place - Certified Venue Professional Designation
2026.EP24.5.s:
An Exhibition Place employee is recognized by the Board for a recent outstanding accomplishment. Andrew Landrigan, Manager-Event Services successfully earned and was presented with his Certified Venue Professional (CVP) designation on August 9th, 2026 at the IAVM Awards Ceremony in Indianapolis. It takes a dedicated person to complete their CVP and Andrew Landrigan, CEM, CVP is the first employee at Exhibition Place to earn this designation.

The Certified Venue Professional (CVP) designation is a distinguished credential that recognizes an individual who has demonstrated operational competence and a deep commitment to the advancement of the venue Management Industry. The CVP designation signifies those venue professionals who have continued to strive for excellence, innovation, and professional growth within venue management. Candidates of the CVP program must also meet compatible experience requirements and successfully complete a comprehensive examination covering the core principles of venue management. A CVP is a distinguished credential and title and assures clients in our very competitive industry that they can be confident you and your team are well prepared to consistently deliver exceptional events.

2026.EP25.1.s:
Toronto, North America’s 4th largest City is home to Exhibition Place. The site currently hosts more than 2,000 events annually with approximately 5.50 million visitors per year for exhibitions, conventions, events, entertainment, sports and other activities. Exhibition Place is evolving into a year-round destination, offering a broad range of events and experiences. The location is accessible and pedestrian-friendly, attracting visitors from local neighborhoods, across Canada, and internationally.

The Exhibition Place Strategic Plan is transitioning from the 2022–2026 framework to a comprehensive, multi-year Exhibition Place Vision Plan, endorsed in principle by the Board of Governors. The Vision Plan will provide a new strategic framework to collaborate with clients, tenants, stakeholders, partners, residents, and visitors to transform Exhibition Place into a more connected, accessible, and vibrant year-round destination.

2027 Budget

On June 1, 2026, Mayor Chow and Budget Chief Councillor Carroll issued budget directions to all City divisions, agencies, boards, and commissions, emphasizing the effective delivery of priority services, long-term financial sustainability, and the identification of operating efficiencies to support a balanced 2027 budget. 2026.EP25.2.t: 2027 Proposed Capital Works Budget as Part of the Ten-Year (2027-2036) Program
2026.EP25.2.s:
Toronto, being North America’s fourth largest City is home to Exhibition Place. The site currently hosts 2,000 events annually with approximately 5.5 million visitors per year for exhibitions, conventions, events, and entertainment, and we are moving towards becoming a 365-day destination for an impressive range of activities. It is important to note that Exhibition Place is pedestrian friendly, and we are visited by our neighbours to the north, from across the country and around the world.

Exhibition Place's vision is to become Canada’s premier destination for conventions, exhibitions, events, and entertainment. We are a unique site in North America, and our goal is to transform Exhibition Place into an intimate space that facilitates unimpeded movement of people.

On June 22, 2026, the City’s Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer provided supplementary instructions for all City Divisions and Agencies with the preparation of the 2027 Capital Works Budget as Part of the Ten-Year Submission.

Supporting the City objective of minimizing debt funding, Exhibition Place staff have worked towards minimizing debt funding for Exhibition Place new projects, also taking into consideration inflationary pressures, and supporting our vision.
